commentary:
Risk tone this morning is two-track: Nvidia's blowout AI-driven sales outlook has Nasdaq futures up 1.1% and the S&P firmer, reinforcing the view that the capex supercycle has legs, while Europe lags — Euro Stoxx Banks off 1.4% and the FTSE lower as fiscal nerves bite. Bund and Buxl futures are sliding, with French OATs underperforming as Paris's borrowing costs have overtaken Rome's on budget and election worries — the structural repricing of term premium, with governments and AI hyperscalers competing for capital, keeps pressure on the long end globally.

The main event is Jackson Hole: Kevin Warsh delivers his first speech as Fed Chair Friday, with markets wary of his inflation approach, a reported Bessent–Warsh split over who sets the price of money, and Trump renewing his bid to oust Lisa Cook. The dollar is recouping losses into it; jobless claims at the lowest since mid-May give little cover for dovishness. In commodities, the softs are the show: arabica coffee is down 3.8% off record highs as Trump's tariff threats on Colombia were withdrawn, robusta following, while cocoa rips 4.4% higher and OJ collapses 6% — a volatile, idiosyncratic complex.

Energy is quieter but the internals matter: Brent holds near $88 with timespreads softening into expiry even as product cracks firm on falling US stockpiles, Hormuz flows keep coming through, and Putin's escalation in Ukraine plus the EU's frozen-asset plan keep a geopolitical bid under TTF (+1.7%) and Henry Hub. Copper and aluminium ease with the softer China tone. Watch Warsh on Friday — the whole rates curve, the dollar and gold trade off it.
